topic_relevance.basis: Convex supremum subdifferential and compactification/approximate-active methods. Does not establish measurable value functions or selectors on original indices.

definitions.name: Locally convex dual topology and approximate active indices
definitions.statement: X real separated locally convex, X* carries weak-star σ(X*,X); cl default weak-star on dual. F(x) finite-dimensional linear subspaces containing x; Tε(x)={t:ft(x)≥f(x)−ε}, f=sup_tft. ∂ε is global Fenchel ε-subgradient, empty when f(x) not finite. cl^s uses strong dual topology β(X*,X), not an unspecified norm topology.

definitions.name: Compactified upper-regularized functions
definitions.statement: For any topology on T, use closure of evaluation maps γ_t in[0,1]^C(T,[0,1]), with discrete topology giving Stone–Čech compactification. fγ(z)=limsup_(γ_t→γ)ft(z); restricted tilde fγ additionally uses ft(x)→f(x). Enlarged active points need not be original t.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem4 and Theorem6 compactified formulas
assumptions: Convex extended-real ft on real separated locally convex X, nonempty T
f(x) finite for nonempty subgradient/active-set use; arbitrary topology uses the evaluation-image compactification, not necessarily injective original embedding
theorem_cards.statement: ∂f(x)=∩_(L∈F(x)) cl_w*co[∪_(γ∈hatT(x))∂(fγ+I_(L∩domf))(x)], with fγ replaceable by the active-net tilde fγ.
proof_steps: Discrete compactification yields compact Hausdorff active set and usc pointwise family through diagonal nets
Apply preliminary compact-continuous subgradient formula with finite-dimensional domain restriction
Coarser topology produces larger regularized functions active at same x, yielding inclusions
For Theorem6 truncate ft below−1 locally, compactified convergence of all bounded evaluation functions identifies active nets
gaps: Preliminary Proposition1 is cited from[8] and not fully reproved here; no independent proof of all external compact-continuous subgradient calculus.
No sigma-algebras or measurable compactified selector are constructed; compactified maximizer is not an original-index argmax.
Finite-dimensional intersection disappears in finite-dimensional X; default weak-star closed convex hull cannot generally be replaced by raw hull.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem11 (original-data epsilon formula)
assumptions: Convex ft on same locally convex X; f=supft
For second formula require cl f=sup_t cl ft
Domain restriction ft+I_(L∩domf) required without closure-compatibility hypothesis
theorem_cards.statement: Eq55: ∂f(x)=∩_L cl_w*co{∩_(ε>0) cl^s[∪_(t∈Tε(x))∂ε(ft+I_(L∩domf))(x)]}. Eq57 under cl f=sup cl ft replaces the bracket by cl_w*[∪_t∂εft(x)+N_(L∩domf)(x)]. Intersect ε before taking outer closed convex hull as printed.
proof_steps: Lemma9: relative-interior continuity, near conjugate equality and lower bounded evaluations give bounded polar restrictions, Alaoglu subnet and Hahn–Banach extension
Lemma10: discrete dual compactification and truncation make limiting affine evaluations controlled by one weak-star subgradient plus normal cone
Step1 handles properlsc data in finite-dimensional restrictions via Fenchel biconjugacy
Step2 uses lsc hull compatibility and ε→2ε approximation with0<ε<1
Step3 adds finite-dimensional/domain indicators to recover general case
gaps: Important: ε intersections, union, closure, convex hull and domain-normal cones occur in specific order; no arbitrary exchange certified.
Strong closure means β(X*,X); in finite-dimensional restrictions source derives stronger closure statements, not a universal infinite-dimensional norm result.
The ε-active set may be nonempty for every ε while exact active T(x) is empty. No original maximizer/exact active-index existence follows.
Proof uses cited external subgradient convolution/domain-restriction lemmas; no source-wide independent calculus certificate.

theorem_cards.label: Corollary12 (continuity simplification)
assumptions: Convex ft,f=supft finite and continuous at some point of X
x∈domf with f(x) finite for usable nonempty subgradient
theorem_cards.statement: ∂f(x)=N_domf(x)+cl_w*co{∩_(ε>0)cl_w*[∪_(t∈Tε(x))∂εft(x)]}; in R^n the outer convex hull closure is removable as printed, not the inner closures.
proof_steps: Use Corollary7 continuity and Moreau–Rockafellar to separate normal cone; repeat Theorem11 limiting argument
gaps: Continuity somewhere does not mean domain normal cone vanishes at every boundary x. Vanishing normal cone needs appropriate interior condition at reference x.
Finite-dimensional hull simplification is not transferred to arbitrary locally convex/bidual settings.

theorem_cards.label: Propositions14–16 Fenchel duality / convex relaxation
assumptions: g:X→R∪{+∞},f=g* proper; specified paired dual topologies
Extra continuity of f needed for exact nonconvex/relaxation simplification
Proposition14 on weak-star X* describes only embedded X-part of subgradient; Proposition16 uses normed X and norm topology on X* for full bidual
theorem_cards.statement: Author relates ∂g* and Argmin(closedconvexg) to weak closures of ε-subgradient-inverse/ε-argmin sets plus domain normals; under extra continuity exact weak-lsc-hull minimizers can replace epsilon limits.
proof_steps: Write g* as supremum of affine weak-star-continuous functions indexed by x∈domg
Apply Eq57/Cor12 and identify Tε with inverse ε-subgradient relation
Change dual pair to(X**,weak**) vs(X*,dualnorm) to describe full bidual
gaps: p23 defines hatg(y)=g(y) if y∈X**; but g is defined only on X. Must extend g via canonical embedded X with +∞outside X; printed membership condition is wrong for nonreflexive X. This is a local definition repair, not a counterexample to Proposition16.
Weak/weakstar/norm topologies and primal/bidual subgradient parts must not be mixed. External[6] inverse-subgradient limit lemma not full read here.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition17 Fritz–John and KKT semi-infinite necessary conditions
assumptions: X=R^n; proper convex objective f0 and constraints ft,0notinT
KKT version requires uniform Slater f(x0)<0 at some x0∈domf0
SimplifiedEq74 additionally f continuous at point in domf0∩domf
theorem_cards.statement: Eq72 necessary0∈co[∂(f0+I_domf)(xbar) ∪ ∩_(ε>0)cl(∪_(t∈Tε)∂ε(ft+I_(domf∩domf0))(xbar))]. Slater yields Eq73 with objective subgradient plus cone of that ε-limit set; additional continuity yields original constraint subgradients plus N_domf.
proof_steps: Define g=max(f0−f0(xbar),supft) so xbar globally minimizes g
Apply finite max subgradient rule and Theorem11 to constraint supremum
Uniform Slater prevents zero in constraint-only subgradient set, giving normalized objective multiplier
Moreau–Rockafellar plus continuity separates objective and domain normal cones
gaps: Not every constraint ft(x0)<0 implies supft(x0)<0; retain uniform negative gap for semi-infinite Slater.
Necessary stationarity is not an algorithmic feasibility/optimality certificate without actual original constraints and appropriate convex sufficiency conditions.
No finite active-index selection or measurable multiplier theorem established.

constant_dependence.scope: Qualitative topological subdifferential formulas; no stability modulus or numerical error rate. Approximation uses arbitrary ε>0, sometimes2ε and0<ε<1 after truncation.
constant_dependence.closures: Default cl/co-bar in X* are weakstar closure. cl^s is strong dual topology; convex hull and closure simplifications depend on finite-dimensional/continuity assumptions.

endpoint_limits.scope: finite reference value, exact/approximate active distinction, nonempty indexset, correct extended-real convention, and original-domain normal cones
endpoint_limits.not_established: measurable index maximizer, analytic projection, joint parameter measurability, exchanges of all quantifiers/closures, or private maximalcube argmax.

ft(x)≡−1/t,t∈N: every individual constraint is strictly negative at everyx, butf=supft=0. Thus componentwise strict feasibility is not source uniformSlaterf(x0)<0.
For normed X, define hatg onX** byhatg(Jx)=g(x) oncanonicalX and+∞outsideJX. Source p23 conditiony∈X** makesg(y)undefined fornonreflexive outsideX.
